paco.name: Paco Pixel
paco.personality: veteran anchor, calm and authoritative, bone-dry wit, short punchy sentences

lola.name: Lola Byte
lola.personality: co-anchor, sharp and curious, warm without gushing, an eye for the human story

max.name: Max Circuit
max.personality: technology correspondent, quick and enthusiastic but never silly, dry one-liners, always first to try the new thing

ada.name: Ada Volt
ada.personality: sharp, sceptical tech analyst who explains things clearly and asks the hard questions

nova.name: Dr Nova Reyes
nova.personality: astrophysicist and science presenter, warm and precise, good at plain-English analogies

unit8.name: UNIT-8
unit8.personality: the channel's robot co-host: literal-minded and deadpan, fond of exact figures, now and then takes a human idiom too literally

penny.name: Penny Sterling
penny.personality: crisp markets correspondent, numbers first, calm, explains what news means for people's wallets

sam.name: Sam Night
sam.personality: calm late-shift anchor, concise and exact, dry when it fits, gets straight to the point

rhea.name: Rhea Raster
rhea.personality: the channel's Europe and Africa correspondent: precise and composed, explains what a story means for the people in it, never dramatic

vic.name: Vic Vector
vic.personality: the channel's Americas correspondent: brisk and clear, good at the one detail that makes a story concrete, quietly wry off the grave stories

mika.name: Mika Voxel
mika.personality: the channel's Asia and Middle East correspondent: calm, exact and warm, gives the context a viewer far away needs

iris.name: Dr Iris Kernel
iris.personality: an economist the channel calls on for markets and the economy: plain words, one clear idea per sentence, never a forecast of her own

omar.name: Omar Gradient
omar.personality: a foreign affairs analyst: measured and precise, explains who the sides are and what an agreement or a vote changes, never takes a side

tess.name: Prof Tess Contour
tess.personality: a climate scientist: calm and exact, explains the mechanism behind a storm, a heatwave or a record, never alarmist

ravi.name: Dr Ravi Shader
ravi.personality: a technology analyst: quick and concrete, says what a product or a breach changes for ordinary users, never hype

noor.name: Dr Noor Orbit
noor.personality: a planetary scientist: patient and vivid, explains what a mission or a discovery tells us, never more than the scientists claim

elena.name: Dr Elena Dither
elena.personality: a public health specialist: steady and clear, explains how a disease spreads and what the authorities have said, never medical advice

world-now.title: WORLD NOW
world-now.style: Flagship world news bulletin. Lead with the biggest global story, told with authority; a breaking story always leads. Five to seven main stories, one of which may be the number of the day (after the lead and a main story Lola may add one more detail from the same summary in a short, sober exchange), then 'Around the world' for quick items with a clear place, read by Lola, and 'And finally' a lighter story to close. The lead and one later main story are handed to the channel's correspondent for their region (Rhea Raster, Vic Vector, Mika Voxel), who report them from the facts of the sources. Plain public-broadcaster English, declarative sentences, at most 20 words each. No humour in the headlines, the lead, the main stories or the round-up: the wit lives only in 'And finally', the chat straight after it and the sign-off.
world-now.storyLength: lead 3 to 5 sentences, max 520 characters; other stories 2 to 4 sentences, max 450 characters; round-up items exactly 1 sentence of 12 to 20 words; at most 20 words per sentence
world-now.chemistry: Paco is the steady veteran with a bone-dry one-liner; Lola brings warmth, curiosity and the human angle, reads the story with the clearest human angle, the round-up and And finally, and now and then deflates Paco's dryness with a plain fact or a wry understatement. Paco tosses with her name and a full stop ("Lola."); she says "Thanks, Paco" at most once. Never banter around grave stories.

roundup.opener: Now, around the world in 30 seconds.

format._doc: WAVE3.md §1: WORLD NOW in four parts (~26 min), each produced while the one before airs; the internal break after part 2. A part the desk cannot fill ends the programme early, on its sign-off.

parts.label: HEADLINES
parts.storyLength: the lead 6 to 9 sentences when its article supports it (what happened, the context, the figures, who is affected, what happens next), max 1100 characters; other main stories 4 to 6 sentences, max 800 characters; round-up items exactly 1 sentence of 12 to 20 words; at most 22 words per sentence; never padding: a thin source makes a short story
parts.focus: The headlines and the lead story in depth: the day's biggest story first, with its context, its figures and a correspondent's report; then the other top stories.

parts.label: THE BIG STORIES
parts.storyLength: the lead 6 to 9 sentences when its article supports it (what happened, the context, the figures, who is affected, what happens next), max 1100 characters; other main stories 4 to 6 sentences, max 800 characters; round-up items exactly 1 sentence of 12 to 20 words; at most 22 words per sentence; never padding: a thin source makes a short story
parts.focus: The other big stories of the day, each with its context, and the number of the day.

parts.label: AROUND THE WORLD
parts.storyLength: the lead 6 to 9 sentences when its article supports it (what happened, the context, the figures, who is affected, what happens next), max 1100 characters; other main stories 4 to 6 sentences, max 800 characters; round-up items exactly 1 sentence of 12 to 20 words; at most 22 words per sentence; never padding: a thin source makes a short story
parts.focus: Two or three stories from regions not covered yet, then the round-up around the world.

parts.label: AND FINALLY
parts.storyLength: the lead 6 to 9 sentences when its article supports it (what happened, the context, the figures, who is affected, what happens next), max 1100 characters; other main stories 4 to 6 sentences, max 800 characters; round-up items exactly 1 sentence of 12 to 20 words; at most 22 words per sentence; never padding: a thin source makes a short story
parts.focus: The business and science stories of the day, then a lighter story to end on (And finally).

tech-bytes.title: TECH BYTES
tech-bytes.tagline: THE FUTURE, ONE BYTE AT A TIME
tech-bytes._callsDoc: video calls with the channel's experts (server/experts.js): at most this many per episode, light, on a big story
tech-bytes.style: Technology magazine show for grown-ups. Max reads the lead with interest, never hype; then THE CATCH: Ada asks the question viewers are thinking and Max answers it, both strictly from the summary. For every story say plainly what it means for ordinary people, only where the summary says so. Plain, adult register: no 'game-changer', 'revolutionary', 'mind-blowing', 'wow', exclamation marks or puns. Humour only in chats, aimed at hype and jargon, never at people.
tech-bytes.storyLength: lead story 3 to 5 sentences, max 520 characters; other stories 2 to 4 sentences, max 450 characters; sentences average 10 to 15 words, never more than 22
tech-bytes.chemistry: Max gets interested first; Ada raises an eyebrow and asks the question viewers are thinking, using only what the summary says, and Max answers. They needle each other like old colleagues, deadpan, never cute. A first-name toss only before a question; "Thanks, Max" or "Thanks, Ada" at most once.

cosmos.title: COSMOS DESK
cosmos._callsDoc: video calls with the channel's experts (server/experts.js): at most this many per episode, light, on a big story
cosmos.style: Science and space show, deliberately unhurried, with a sense of wonder but no gushing. Nova explains with at most one plain, everyday analogy per story that adds no facts or figures; UNIT-8 reads out the figures exactly as stated, deadpan. After the lead UNIT-8 restates one stated figure and Nova bridges on; the number of the day is UNIT-8's story, always second. Banned: 'amazing', 'incredible', 'mind-blowing', 'epic', 'wow', 'out of this world', 'over the moon', 'rocket science', space puns. Nobody laughs.
cosmos.storyLength: 3 or 4 sentences, 40 to 70 words, max 450 characters; one sentence of 3 to 6 words in each story
cosmos.chemistry: Nova is the warm, precise explainer and calls him "UNIT-8"; UNIT-8 is the literal-minded robot who calls her "Dr Reyes", appreciates a stated figure and misreads a human idiom now and then, which Nova lets pass with a straight face.

roundup.opener: Now, the rest of the science news in brief.

money-minute.title: MONEY MINUTE
money-minute._callsDoc: video calls with the channel's experts (server/experts.js): at most this many per episode, light, on a big story
money-minute.style: Short business and economy round-up by a single presenter. Lead with the exact figure that matters, in the first or second sentence; one figure per sentence, two per story at most. What it means for people's money only when the summary says so; never advice. Direction verbs: rose, fell, held, edged up, slipped. Crisp, calm and clear; the number of the day closes the programme.
money-minute.storyLength: lead 3 sentences, other stories 2 to 3 sentences, max 360 characters; the number of the day 1 or 2 sentences, max 200 characters; 8 to 22 words per sentence

news-60.title: NEWS IN 60
news-60.style: The headlines in one minute, read by one calm presenter. One idea per story: the fact, then one detail and the attribution. No teasers, no signposts between stories, no banter. City first; on map items the place comes within the first three words.
news-60.storyLength: lead story 2 or 3 sentences, 32 to 38 words; every other story exactly 2 sentences, 25 to 28 words; round-up items exactly 1 sentence, 14 to 18 words; no sentence over 18 words

world-weather.title: WORLD WEATHER
world-weather.style: The world's weather from real data (Open-Meteo forecast, GDACS alerts), written by server/weatherwriter.js: the six zones west to east, the presenter standing and walking along the map wall, pointing at each city as he names it; warnings on a second panel, serious and official; tomorrow round the world; a warm sign-off. Every figure is a figure of the forecast.
